details: hijiko-parser@1.0.0 ships no functionality — its entire index.js is a single console.log line and it declares no lifecycle or bin scripts — and exists only to install a dependency from a non-registry host. Its dependencies map (repeated in npm-shrinkwrap.json, so the pin survives lockfile-based installs) points marker-script-suffix-mapper@1.0.18 at a raw plain-HTTP tarball URL: hxxp://web[.]vitemaweed[.]fr:4873/marker-script-suffix-mapper/-/marker-script-suffix-mapper-1[.]0[.]18[.]tgz. Installing this package makes npm fetch and execute the install lifecycle of a tarball served from web[.]vitemaweed[.]fr:4873 instead of registry[.]npmjs[.]org, bypassing the registry's integrity and audit trail. The package has an empty description, no repository, and no README.
